details.description: DeepSeek-R1 is DeepSeek AI's first-generation reasoning model, trained primarily through large-scale reinforcement learning and producing chain-of-thought output for math, coding and logic tasks; DeepSeek states it "achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1 across math, code, and reasoning tasks." It is a 671-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with about 37 billion parameters active per token, released January 20, 2025 under the MIT license. AWS offers it as a fully managed, serverless model on Amazon Bedrock with a 128K-token context window. DeepSeek's own website now lists R1 only in its research/model history section behind the newer V3, V3.1, V3.2, V4 and V4.1 families, and DeepSeek's current API pricing page no longer lists an R1/deepseek-reasoner endpoint among its current models.
advantages: Scores 79.8% pass@1 on AIME 2024 and 97.3% pass@1 on MATH-500 (Hugging Face model card).
Scores 84.0% on MMLU-Pro and 65.9% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench (Hugging Face model card).
DeepSeek reports a Codeforces rating of 2029 for the model (Hugging Face model card).

AWS states it is "the first cloud service provider to deliver DeepSeek-R1 as a fully managed, generally available model," with data-privacy protections stating inputs and outputs are not shared with model providers (AWS Bedrock announcement).
disadvantages: Superseded within DeepSeek's own model lineup by the V3, V3.1, V3.2, V4 and V4.1 families, and no longer listed as a current model on DeepSeek's own API pricing page (deepseek.com; api-docs.deepseek.com).
Knowledge cutoff of January 2025, per AWS's Bedrock model card.
Text-only: no image, audio or video input or output support (AWS Bedrock model card).
use_cases: Multi-step logical reasoning and chain-of-thought explanations

sources.title: DeepSeek-R1 now available as a fully managed, serverless model in Amazon Bedrock

notes: Catalog facts show max_input_tokens 128000 and max_output_tokens [4096, 8192]; AWS's current Bedrock model card states a 128K context window and 8K max output tokens, matching the catalog's upper bound, so no correction was needed. DeepSeek's own site and API docs no longer surface R1/deepseek-reasoner as a current model, though AWS's Bedrock model card still lists its lifecycle as 'Active' with EOL no sooner than 2026-03-10; both statuses are reported above rather than reconciled, since they come from different parties (maker vs. host).
